To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the baroreflexes in the renal hypertensive and medial sclerctic rabbits were set to a high pressure level and had a high gain.
the carotid baroreceptor control of the circulation is modified in experimental renal hypertension and medial sclerosis.
the carotid baroreceptor reflex control of the circulation in renal hypertensive and medial sclerocitic rabbits was modified by the aortic baroreceptors and by the disease process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reflex control of the circulation in the rabbit by the carotidsinus baroreceptors in experimental hypertension and medial sclerosis.

the role of the carotid sinuses and aortic baroreceptors in the reflex regulation of blood pressure, and in the control of vascular resistance in normal rabbits (N) and those with experimental renal hypertension (RH) or medial sclerotic nephritis (MS).
the role of the baroreflex system in maintaining blood pressure in the face of a chronic elevation of pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the baroreflex control of blood pressure and hindquarter vascular resistance is enhanced and set to a higher level in the renal hypertensive and medial sclerotics.
the carotid baroreceptor reflex is altered in the MS and renal hypertensive rabbit.
the reflexes from the carotid baroreceptors are altered in renal and sclerotic hypertension, but the changes are different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the baroreceptors of the carotid and aortic sinuses are capable of maintaining a normal relationship between blood pressure, vascular resistance, and heart rate in the face of the elevated blood pressure of renal hypertension.
the reflex control of the circulation by the carotids is different in renal hypertension than in the other two groups, and that the aortic nerves have a different effect in renal hypertension.

the reflex control of the circulation in renal hypertensive and medial sclerotics was modified by the aortic baroreceptors and by the disease itself, and that the changes in the reflex control of vascular resistance were more important than those in heart rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the presence of hypertension, the baroreflexes become more efficient in terms of the amount of blood pressure change produced for a given change in baroreceptor firing rate.
in the renal hypertension and sclerotic rabbits, the carotid baroreceptors have a greater influence on the vascular resistance than on heart rate.
the carotid baroreceptors were able to control the blood pressure and vascular resistance in the MS and the RH rabbits.
